title: Fix bug where field is not returned if it has the same prefix as a nested field

timeline.message: Fix bug where field is not returned if it has the same prefix as a nested field
timeline.author: iverase

timeline.body:
We currently only check if a field starts with the same characters as a nested prefix but we do not check that the next character of the field is a path separator ('.'). This commit updates the check to make sure we distinguish between a nested path and a field with the same nested prefix.

fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/82905

timeline.author: iverase

timeline.body: nit: with checkstyle rules these large XContentBuilder setups are hard to read. I'm wondering if we can use the new Java text blocks to create the mapping from a readable String representation, but then again I haven't found a quick example after some searching just now. Happy to leave it as is for now but if you have an idea how to remedy this I'd be glad to see and copy going forward.

timeline.body: Looks good to me, maybe @romseygeek has some comments on directly checking the field separator though because he is currently working on allowing dots in fields names. As far as I understand this should be okay here though, just checking for making sure...

reply.body: This is fine for now. I have a PR which simplifies some of this nested path handling which I think will help here as well in the longer term (#75677) but the newly added test should ensure that things work correctly.

timeline.body: Thanks for fixing this, LGTM but I would like a quick check from @romseygeek if the direct use of the field separator is okay going forward for the work he is currently doing with dots in fieldnames.
